failure_modes.description: Vehicle platoons cannot be reliably detected at intersections
failure_modes.evidence: Vehicle detection systems have significant limitations in accurately identifying platoons, especially in mixed traffic conditions with varying vehicle sizes, speeds, and driver behaviors

failure_modes.description: Traffic patterns do not have sufficient predictability over short distances
failure_modes.evidence: Empirical studies show traffic patterns are highly chaotic with limited predictability beyond 30-60 seconds, making the claimed coordination window unrealistic

failure_modes.description: Slime mold behavior cannot meaningfully map to traffic systems
failure_modes.evidence: Comparing slime mold pressure waves to traffic signal coordination is a false analogy - biological systems operate under fundamentally different constraints and principles

failure_modes.description: Adaptive traffic signal coordination already exists
failure_modes.evidence: Systems like SCATS, SCOOT, and RHODES already implement adaptive signal coordination based on real-time traffic data

failure_modes.description: The system would create worse overall traffic flow
failure_modes.evidence: Optimizing for platoons inevitably creates bottlenecks at intersection boundaries, increasing overall travel time for the majority of vehicles not in organized platoons
Real-time communication between all neighboring intersections would require massive infrastructure investment and maintenance, making implementation impractical
